notice: DRAFT, NOT REVIEWED. An agent wrote these one-line statements on 2026-10-20 by paraphrasing barrier themes in published accessibility progress reports (sources below). Each label is the priority area under which the SOURCE ORGANIZATION itself placed the theme (labelBasis says how). No passage is copied and no figure is taken over. Before this set is run for numbers or quoted anywhere, a human checks every statement against its source, fixes or deletes rows, sets "status" to "reviewed", adds their name to "reviewedBy" and renames the file to public-silver.json (eval/README.md). Until then `npm run eval -- --set silver` refuses to run; `--draft-check` only checks that the file goes through the harness and saves nothing.

labelBasis.feedback-theme-by-area: The organization's Feedback section groups this theme under the priority area.
labelBasis.area-section: The theme appears in the organization's section for that priority area (a barrier table, or a barrier named next to an action).
labelBasis.org-category-mapped: The organization used its own category name (for example 'physical spaces' or 'technology'); we mapped that name to the ACA key. Check these first.

statements.text: Employees with disabilities see little chance to move up in their careers.
The hiring process is hard to get through for people whose disability can't be seen.
Nobody has explained how going back to the office and hybrid work will affect my accessibility needs.

statements.section: Feedback > What We Heard > Built environment
statements.text: Some of the buildings we work in are not accessible.

statements.section: Feedback > What We Heard > Built environment
statements.text: Getting into and around the parking lot at work is difficult.

statements.section: Feedback > What We Heard > Built environment
statements.text: There is not enough accessible parking close to the workplace.

statements.section: Feedback > What We Heard > Built environment
statements.text: The motion-sensor doors don't open reliably, while doors with a button always work.

statements.section: Feedback > What We Heard > Built environment
statements.text: The adaptive equipment I need is often not available at the workplace.
There are not enough lockers available at the workplace.
The secure doors at work need automatic buttons and card readers that everyone can use.
Some of the IT support services are not accessible.
Some apps and web pages can't be used with assistive technology.
The read-aloud feature in the chat tool only works after a message is sent, not while I write it.
I can't use a dark mode to read information on screen.
The internal web pages and applications we have to use are not accessible.
Documents and PDFs are shared in formats that are not accessible.
The news shown on the screens in our building has no captions.
Businesses owned or led by people with disabilities get few chances to win contracts.
Our office spaces are not sensory-friendly and can't be adjusted to different needs.
Doors and workspaces in some locations are hard to use.
Emails sent by different parts of the department are not accessible.
The online client account is hard to find my way around.
Nobody explains the assistive technologies we already have, so people don't know they exist.

statements.section: Feedback > client feedback > Theme 1 (links to Priority area 6)
statements.text: With my mobility limits I need banking services I can use from home instead of going to a branch.

statements.section: Feedback > client feedback > Theme 1 (links to Priority area 6)
statements.text: Staff need more training to help clients with disabilities.

statements.section: Feedback > client feedback > Theme 3 (links to Priority area 2)
statements.text: The branch needs more places to sit and more accessible parking spaces.

statements.section: Feedback > client feedback > Theme 3 (links to Priority area 2)
statements.text: Clients with disabilities wait too long for help at the branch.
The fluorescent lights at work are a problem for me.
The scent-free rule at the office is not enforced.
Leaders don't know which accessible technology options exist.
New and current employees need better onboarding to learn the accessible technology we have.
It is hard to get an ASL or LSQ interpreter when I visit a branch.
Getting my bank statements in an alternate format takes too long.

statements.section: 2.6 Design and Delivery of Programs and Services (barrier table)
statements.text: The card number and phone number on my card are printed too small and not raised, so I can't read them with low vision.

statements.section: 2.6 Design and Delivery of Programs and Services (barrier table)
statements.text: The phone system doesn't give me enough time to enter my credit card number.

statements.section: 2.6 Design and Delivery of Programs and Services (barrier table)
statements.text: The phone menu is hard to get through with buttons, and it is hard to reach a live agent.

statements.section: 2.6 Design and Delivery of Programs and Services (barrier table)
statements.text: Putting in a travel notice on the online portal is hard to do with accessibility tools.
Some office meeting rooms make it hard to join video meetings.
Resources about accessibility requests are hard to get, and people leaders don't know how to support them.
The workplace accommodation process is not the same from one team to the next.
Asking for assistive technology at work needs better support.
The internal careers site is hard to use with accessibility tools when I search and apply for jobs.

statements.section: Procurement of Goods, Services and Facilities
statements.text: The platform and training documents suppliers have to use are not accessible.

statements.section: Design and Delivery of Programs and Services
statements.text: The rules for who can get the accessibility discount are hard to understand.

statements.section: Design and Delivery of Programs and Services
statements.text: Store staff can't easily find accessibility information to help customers.
The payment terminals in the workplace cafeteria are not accessible.

statements.section: Design and Delivery of Programs and Services
statements.text: There are too few ways to move me between my wheelchair and the aircraft seat.
My folding manual wheelchair can't be stored in the cabin.
My large power wheelchair doesn't fit through the cargo door of the smaller plane.
Pre-boarding times and boarding equipment are not reliable at some airports.
The rules for service dogs, including dogs trained by their owners, are a barrier when I fly.
The washroom on smaller, narrow-body planes is hard to use with a disability.
Getting help when my mobility aid is damaged or delayed on a trip is hard.
The signs and wayfinding in the airport are hard to follow.
The airport has no quiet sensory room to wait in.
The airport elevators are too small or not working.
There are not enough wheelchairs and aisle chairs in the terminal.
Each department handles accommodation requests in its own way.
Onboarding does not support new employees who told us about a disability.
There is no accommodation support before my first day of work.
The website and app are hard to use with assistive technology and for neurodivergent people.
The gate screens don't show captions or sign language for announcements.
The in-flight entertainment has no accessible mode for people with vision loss.
Announcements during the flight have no captions or sign language.
The signs and icons used on the trip are hard to understand.

statements.section: Design and Delivery of Programs and Services > On-board services
statements.text: The service from the cabin crew did not meet the needs of passengers with disabilities.

statements.section: Design and Delivery of Programs and Services > Ground services
statements.text: A weight limit for mobility aids on some aircraft stopped me from bringing my chair.

statements.section: Information and Communication Technologies > Website and mobile app
statements.text: The website and mobile app have accessibility gaps.
